conviction_note: Mild positive lean from an easy tariff-depressed Q3 2025 comp, management's 'potentially exceeding our initial plans', a strong Disguise costume licence and supportive peer/retailer toy data. Against that: the CFO's 'front-weighted' 2026 with no new 2H holiday-theatrical toys, and an 18% 20-day run-up to a 52-week high that already sits at most price targets. The bar is one or two analysts and disagrees across sources, so every finding is capped small. abs_move 8% (no usable chain; median past reaction 5.1%, mean about 8%, largest quarter, thin turnover); p_up 55 gives +0.8, almost the findings' sum of +0.7. That agreement is a coincidence, not a fit.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call (2026-07-23), CEO Berman said JAKKS was on track for 'achieving potentially exceeding our initial plans' for 2026. POS at the top 2 US accounts was positive in H1 (double-digit in Q2), and new product was 'shipping now for fall planogram sets', i.e. into Q3. There is still no numeric guide, so this is tone against a 1-2 analyst EPS bar of $2.02-2.31 (vs $1.80 a year ago).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (revenue +7% vs consensus, tone 'developing as planned'): +2.90%. Q1 2026: +10.57%. Q4 2025: +23.73%. Q3 2025 (EPS $1.80 vs $2.12, revenue -34%): -5.13%. This name has bought beats on the last three prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The words are three months old. They are probably partly in the 18% run-up, but the single estimate was cut ($2.37 to $2.31) after the call rather than raised. If the market fully believed 'exceeding plan', estimates would have gone up, not down.
findings.independence: Same call as the front-weighting finding below (one document, two different facts). Q2 press release: 'good momentum heading into the second half' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm).

findings.finding: CFO Kimble on the same call: 2026 is planned 'a bit more front-weighted than normal given the strength of Super Mario', with 'no new toy introductions in the second half supporting holiday theatrical releases'. So Q3 growth should run below Q2's +17%. Consensus implies about +9% revenue and +12-28% EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, the last time the seasonal quarter disappointed (no theatrical tie-ins, revenue -34%, EPS miss): -5.13%.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up and an EPS bar 12-28% above last year suggest the market is extrapolating H1 strength. If this phasing were priced, the stock would not be at a 52-week high above most $28.50-30 targets.
findings.independence: Same document as the finding above. Quartr summary repeats it (https://quartr.com/events/jakks-pacific-inc-jakk-q2-2026_ozuFuLen).

findings.finding: The Q3 2025 comp is very easy: net sales $211.2M (-34%), Toys/CP $156.1M (-40.9%), US -39.5%, driven by tariff-related cuts to direct-import orders. In 2026 the IEEPA tariffs were struck down and refunded (JAKKS booked $6.8M in Q2), and H1 shipments were over 75% FOB, 'the highest this decade'. The same recovery gave Q2 2026 +17% revenue and a 7% revenue beat. Consensus of about $230M is only +9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the same recovery dynamic (revenue $139.2M vs $129.6M consensus): +2.90%.
findings.why_not_priced: The comp is public, so it is partly priced. The revenue consensus (+9%) sits well below Q2's +17% on the same recovery. If the full recovery were priced, the revenue bar would sit closer to Q2's growth rate. Front-weighting (above) is the counter-reason, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 release with US +24.4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm). Earnings Whispers Q2 revenue beat (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/JAKK). Toy Association on the IEEPA ruling and refunds (https://www.toyassociation.org/PressRoom2/News/2026-News/scotus-strikes-down-ieepa-tariffs-president-trump-issues-new-tariff-proclamation.aspx).

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: JAKK took +2.9% on the Hasbro day. What remains is that a single-analyst bar may not have been updated for it. Proxy only.

findings.finding: Disguise (JAKKS costumes, $55.1M in Q3 2025, -3.8%, about 26% of Q3 sales) has the KPop Demon Hunters costume licence for Halloween 2026, alongside Toy Story 5 and Sonic. Netflix says KPop Demon Hunters was 2025's most in-demand Halloween costume. Spirit Halloween lists it as a top 2026 trend, and Costumes were already +8% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate costume-surprise history. Costumes are about a quarter of Q3 revenue, so the rest (toys, -41% last Q3) has to at least hold flat for this to show in the total.
findings.why_not_priced: The licence is public, but the sell-in size is not. No sell-out or volume data exists in the public record, so this is a proxy sized small and net of the rest of the company.
findings.independence: Netflix Tudum (https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/kpop-demon-hunters-disguise-costumes). Spirit Halloween 2026 trends via NJBIZ (https://njbiz.com/spirit-halloween-2026-costume-trends/). Q2 costumes +8% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1009829/000118518526003108/jakkex10-1.htm).

baseline_tension: No usable skew. The positive lean from documents and proxies runs with the 18% run-up rather than against it, so much of it is plausibly already in the price; that is why p_up is only 55.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar single-source and disagreeing: EPS $2.02-2.31, revenue one rounded $0.23B): capped the reported-quarter findings. 'Exceeding plan' went +1.0 to +0.6, easy comp +1.0 to +0.8, front-weighting -1.0 to -0.8.
Rule 5 (proxies small): peer/retailer read-through +0.5 to +0.3, because JAKK already took +2.9% on the Hasbro day.
Rule 9 (segment net of rest): the KPop Demon Hunters costume finding went +0.5 to +0.4, as costumes are only about 26% of Q3 sales.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked at about 4%, not crowded. The run-up negative was trimmed -1.0 to -0.7 because the reaction history shows beats bought on the last three prints.
Rule 3 (read the set): the two Q2-call findings share one document but are compatible (strong year, H1-weighted), so both are kept and the shared source is noted in independence.
